sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Build and server settings
sections.what: Sets the build tool's options: the add-ons to load, the folder mappings, the output folder, and the local development server, including forwarding API requests during local development outside Replit.
sections.why: The comments explain the API forwarding is for local development outside Replit. The other reasons are not stated.
sections.watch_out: The output folder is emptied on every build, so files must not be stored there by hand.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Preview server and API forwarding settings
sections.what: On a local computer, requests that start with /api are passed on to a separate API server, so the web page and the API look like one site. The preview server listens on the configured port on all network addresses and accepts any host name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Replit hosting platform already routes /api traffic itself, so the proxy is only added for local runs where the start command sets the target.
sections.watch_out: Setting allowedHosts to true accepts requests for any host name, which is fine on a local machine but unsafe if the preview server is reachable from outside.

summary: The configuration for the Vite build tool that builds and serves the capital projects app.
purpose: Tells the build tool which add-ons to load, where source and output live, how web addresses map to folders, and how the local development server behaves.
why: Partly stated: the comments say that local development outside Replit forwards API requests to another server. Likely reason for the Replit-only add-ons: the app runs on Replit. The rest is not stated.
how: It reads the port, API proxy target and base path from the environment. It loads the React and Tailwind add-ons, and loads the Replit add-ons only outside production and only when running on Replit. It maps the @ shortcut to the src folder, sets the output folder to dist/public, and starts a development server on all network interfaces.
inputs: The PORT, API_PROXY_TARGET, BASE_PATH, NODE_ENV and REPL_ID environment variables, and the source files.
outputs: The built web files in dist/public, and the running development server.
risks: The development server accepts all hostnames and turns off strict file access, which is loose if it is ever exposed beyond development. The output folder is emptied on every build. A non-numeric PORT value is not checked.
debug: If the page is blank or API calls fail, check API_PROXY_TARGET and the port. If @ imports fail, check the alias. If the build output is missing, check the dist/public path. The second half of this file is not shown, so later settings are not covered here.
